title: Justice and Faith -- Ch. 5: Profiles of Supreme Court Justices
primary_topics: Chapter 5 of 'Justice and Faith' -- CJP's master-of-ceremonies introductions of the ten then-sitting Supreme Court justices at Justice Justo P. Torres Jr.'s retirement rites on October 22, 1997, each one delivered as the justice rose to present the honoree with a memento of his term per a 'hallowed tradition'

A miniature collective portrait of the 1997 Supreme Court bench -- vignettes of judicial style, temperament, and signature virtues for Puno, Vitug, Romero, Francisco, Mendoza, Kapunan, Melo, Bellosillo, Davide, and Torres -- that doubles as CJP's own taxonomy of magistracy

An extended tribute to Justice Torres as honoree -- appointment by President Ramos on March 13, 1996, the running 'lucky number 13' motif, his 'head-on activist' temperament, and the Court-of-Appeals-to-SC trajectory -- closing with a Filipino-language family-of-virtues paragraph for CJ Davide as the rhetorical peak
sub_topics: The hallowed retirement-rite tradition -- each justice formally presents to the honoree 'a memento of his term, something he had used to discharge his function as a jurist'
Composition note: only ten justices introduced because Padilla and Hermosisima had retired and Narvasa and Regalado were abroad on official business; introductions ordered by program sequence
Puno vignette -- 'trained surgeon,' 'laser-like precision,' 'populist causes and libertarian ideals,' Holmes-like lonely battles through stirring dissents
Vitug vignette -- 'icon of the academe,' 'ultimate teacher and compassionate friend,' subtlety and rationality of law in cadenced expression
Romero vignette -- 'the gracious and precious gem of the Court, its only lady member,' tenacious in forensic combat against chauvinistic colleagues
Francisco vignette -- law as 'a jealous master,' 'never winces or falters,' 'the quiet comfort of a disciplined conscience' as the single standard
Mendoza vignette -- 'classic jurist molded in the ivy-league traditions of Yale,' scholarly/well-researched/cerebral/lofty/impeccable ponencias
Kapunan vignette -- 'perfect gentleman of the bench,' suave/noble, firm believer in rule of law, indefatigable but never imperious
Melo vignette -- 'consensus builder' and 'living barometer of (the Court's) leanings,' respected for objectivity, fairness, lucidity, openness
Bellosillo vignette -- 'paragon, the pith and soul of the career magistrate,' quick to spot lesions but adept at defending lower-court welfare; diligent, methodical, single-minded
Davide vignette -- Tagalog cadence: 'makabayan, maginoo, marangal, matapang, masipag, mapagkakatiwalaan, may mabuting asal at diwa...' -- the epitome of the Filipino jurist

Torres tribute (the longest) -- March 13, 1996 Ramos appointment; the 13-13-13 running joke (Torres ranked 13th in CA seniority and 13th in SC seniority; his father 13th in the 1925 bar); 'only important place where he is not Number Thirteen is in the heart of Rose, where he is Number One'; 'head-on activist...canalized neither by tradition nor by precedent,' valedictory address closer
signature_phrases: Like a trained surgeon, he uses his pen with laser-like precision to separate and excise fabrication from truth and pretension from reality

the perfect gentleman of the bench, suave, noble
the consensus builder of the Court and the living barometer of its leanings and positions

thirteen is the lucky number of Justice Tito. The only important place where he is not Number Thirteen is in the heart of Rose, where he is Number One and only!
the labyrinth of his vibrant mind and indomitable spirit in the judicial cosmos

stances.claim: The members of the Supreme Court are best honored not by laudatory abstractions but by precisely-drawn vignettes that name each one's signature judicial virtue -- surgeon-precision, academe-icon, gracious gem, jealous-master magistrate, ivy-league scholar, perfect gentleman, consensus builder, career-magistrate paragon, and Filipino-virtue epitome.
stances.rhetorical_move: ceremonial-portraiture: each introduction is a one-paragraph judicial epigram

stances.claim: CJ Davide is the epitome of the Filipino jurist -- the Tagalog catalogue of virtues (makabayan, maginoo, marangal, matapang, masipag, mapagkakatiwalaan, may mabuting asal at diwa, may pagpapahalaga sa kapwa) -- and his profile is given as the rhetorical peak of the introductions.
stances.rhetorical_move: language-shift: switch to Tagalog at the chief's profile to mark him as the Filipino ideal

stances.claim: Justice Torres's retirement is a story of '13' as lucky number -- he ranked 13th at the CA, 13th at the SC, his father ranked 13th in the 1925 bar -- yet in his wife Rose's heart he is Number One; the running motif is the speech's organizing joke.
stances.rhetorical_move: playful-coincidence: a single numerical motif used to unify a biographical sketch

stances.claim: Judicial excellence has multiple legitimate models -- the dissenter (Puno), the teacher (Vitug), the gentleman (Kapunan), the consensus-builder (Melo), the career magistrate (Bellosillo), the scholar (Mendoza), the disciplined-conscience magistrate (Francisco), the lady tenacious (Romero), the activist (Torres), the Filipino ideal (Davide) -- the bench is plural, not monolithic.
stances.rhetorical_move: pluralist-portraiture: each profile names a distinct excellence

notable_anecdotes: Lucky-13 running motif on Torres -- appointed March 13, 1996; ranked 13th in CA seniority before elevation and 13th in SC seniority on retirement; his father, Justo Sr., ranked 13th in the 1925 bar -- relieved only by Rose's heart, where he is 'Number One and only'
The hallowed memento tradition -- each justice presents the honoree with a personal symbol of office at the retirement rite, with CJP's introductions framing each handover
Composition note as integral to the script -- Padilla and Hermosisima already retired; Narvasa and Regalado abroad; the bench is therefore introduced as ten, not fourteen
Davide-as-rhetorical-peak -- CJP switches into Tagalog precisely at the Chief's profile, signaling that the catalogue of Filipino virtues is the speech's climax
Puno-as-Holmes -- CJP places Puno in the Holmes lineage of lonely dissents, the only justice given a comparator from American jurisprudence
target_audience: The audience at Justice Torres's retirement rites -- bench, bar, family, and Court personnel -- at the October 22, 1997 program
Future Justice-and-Faith readers tracking the 1997 SC bench in CJP's own portraiture

one_paragraph_summary: Chapter 5 of 'Justice and Faith' reproduces CJP's master-of-ceremonies introductions of the then-sitting members of the Supreme Court at Justice Justo P. Torres Jr.'s retirement rites on October 22, 1997 -- each delivered as the named justice rose, per a 'hallowed tradition,' to present the honoree with a memento of his term. Only ten justices are introduced because Padilla and Hermosisima had retired and Narvasa and Regalado were abroad on official business. The vignettes are deliberately plural: Puno is 'a trained surgeon' wielding 'laser-like precision' and waging Holmes-like lonely dissents; Vitug is 'an icon of the academe' whose restrained language renders law in 'cadenced expression'; Romero, 'the gracious and precious gem of the Court, its only lady member,' tenaciously battles 'sometimes chauvinistic colleagues'; Francisco is 'the essential magistrate' guided solely by 'the quiet comfort of a disciplined conscience'; Mendoza is 'molded in the ivy-league traditions of Yale,' scholarly and impeccable; Kapunan is 'the perfect gentleman of the bench,' firm but never imperious; Melo is 'the consensus builder' and 'the living barometer' of the Court; Bellosillo is 'the paragon, the pith and soul of the career magistrate,' diligent and methodical; and at the rhetorical climax CJP shifts into Tagalog to name Davide 'the epitome of the Filipino jurist -- makabayan, maginoo, marangal, matapang, masipag, mapagkakatiwalaan.' The longest introduction is reserved for the honoree, Justice Torres, whose March 13, 1996 Ramos appointment is woven into a 'lucky 13' running joke (CA seniority 13, SC seniority 13, his father Justo Sr. 13th in the 1925 bar), softened only by Rose's heart, where 'he is Number One and only'; the closing invites the audience to rise for Torres's valedictory.
